title: Annotatio I §.III close: Circumcision and Passover institutions predicate improperly — stop before Baptism/Cup
pass_a_gloss: For when (a) in the Institution of Circumcision God addresses Abraham thus: This is my covenant between me and you and your seed after you, which you shall keep, that every male among you be circumcised, Gen. 17:10, God’s covenant is predicated of circumcision only improperly: For Circumcision is not properly the covenant but the sign of the covenant, God Himself interpreting in the next verse 11: You shall cut off the foreskin of the flesh, and this itself shall be the sign of the covenant between me and you. When (b) in the Institution of the Passover Moses in God’s name informs the whole people: The lamb to be eaten by you in the manner of those hastening is the Lord’s passover, Exod. 12:11; also: Take a lamb each householder for his family and slaughter the passover, v. 21; also: if anyone of you, while they eat the slaughtered lamb, asks what thing or office you are performing here? You shall answer: it is the Passover sacrifice of the Lord passing over the sons of Israel in Egypt, v. 27 — in all these propositions passover or passage is enunciated only improperly both of the lamb and of the slaughter and eating of the lamb, the substance of the lamb by no means to be converted into a transient action by any proper predication, and indeed by the same species of trope by which in the N.T. Christ Himself is called our passover, 1 Cor. 5:7, and also the rock that followed the Israelites in the desert: For a thing that signifies is wont to be named by the name of the thing it signifies, as it is written, the seven ears are seven years and many such. Hence it is that it was said the rock was Christ: for he did not say the rock signifies Christ, but as if this were so! Assuredly it was not this by substance but by signification — Augustine’s words, Questions on Leviticus 57.
pass_b_english: (a) In circumcision’s Institution (Gen. 17:10–11) God’s covenant is predicated of circumcision only improperly — circumcision is the sign of the covenant, God Himself explaining in the next verse.

(b) In the Passover Institution (Exod. 12:11, 21, 27) passover / passage is predicated only improperly of the lamb and of its slaughter and eating — the same species of trope by which Christ is our passover (1 Cor. 5:7) and the desert rock was Christ by signification, not substance (Augustine, Quaest. Lev. 57).
Stop before §.III continuation (Baptism and Cup Institution inductions; SPECIFICA genus).
source_text: Quando enim (a) in Institutione Circumcisionis, Deus ita Abrahamum alloquitur: Hoc est foedus meum inter me & inter vos & semen tuum post te, quod servabis, ut circumcidatur vobis omnis mas Gen. 17, 10. foedus Dei de circumcisione non nisi impropriè praedicatur: Neque enim Circumcisio propriè foedus est, sed signum foederis, Deô ipsômet interprete versu proximè sequente 11. Debetis autem praeputium carnis praescindere, hocque ipsum foederis signum futurum est inter me & vos. Quando (b) in Institutione Paschatos, totum populum, Moses, nomine Dei, ita, informat: Agnus à vobis, in star festinantium, comedendus, est pascha Domini, Exod. 12, 11. item: Accipite agnum quilibet paterfamilias pro familia sua & mactate pascha, versu 21. Item: si quis ex vobis, agno mactato vescentibus, quaesiverit: quid rei seu officii hic peragitis? Respondebitis: est Pascha sacrificium Domini filios Israelis praetereuntis in Egypto, vers. 27. in propositionibus hisce cunctis, pascha, seu transitus, tam de agno, quàm de mactatione & comesione agni, nonnisi impropriè enunciatur, substantiâ agni nequaquam in actionem transeuntem, per praedicationem aliquam propriam, convertendâ, & quidem per ejusdem speciei tropum, per quem in N. T. ipse Christus pascha nostrum dicitur 1. Cor. 5. vers. 7. nec non petra, Israelitas in deserto secuta: Solet enim res quae significat, ejus rei nomine, quam significat, nuncupari, sicut scriptum est, septem spicae septem anni sunt & multa hujusmodi. Hinc est quod dictum est petra erat Christus: non enim dixit: petra significat Christum, sed tanquam hoc esset! Utique per substantiam hoc non erat, sed per significationem, sunt verba Augustini, quaest. supra Levit. 57.
